I think the first word is "Mada." [Interpretation] "Even though the municipality assembly of Kljuc at its session held on the 10th of April, 1991 had confirmed its existence" -- [In English] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, I think it would be easier if it's translated by an interpreter or a translator who under Rule 73 has been sworn specifically to the effect of doing that particular duty, honestly. And I'm not saying that the witness will not. But obviously I would imagine you are a qualified historian. They Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. are qualified translators. And I would rather opt for them to translate it direct to us in English and in French and proceed from there. After all, this is not a document that has been prepared by Dr. Donia. It's an official document, as I understand it, and I do not expect Dr. Donia to translate it for us or to read it, because it's -- Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the people in the translation booth are more comfortable having someone read it and then translate it, I do have a translator sitting here. She would be happy to just read it as best she can, if that's more convenient for them. I'm just offering that. It makes no difference to me how we do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Mr. Ackerman. What do you prefer?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I think from my experience the interpreters prefer that it's read, because that is their function. They could easily read this in, but I think it's better that somebody reads it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I take your offer, Mr. Ackerman, and I think the lady can proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Do I have to stand or sit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, you can sit. And read it slowly so it is simultaneously translated into the two officials languages of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first word is illegible. It's probably "even though" -- "the municipal assembly of Kljuc held at its session held on the 10th of April, 1991 had confirmed its existence and expressed its decision to remain within the community of municipalities of Banja Luka and elected its representatives to the community assembly, and because of the earlier transformation of this community into a regional community, "Bosanska Krajina," or Bosnian Krajina, and after that became the autonomous region of Bosnian Krajina, and the recently completed plebiscite of the Serbian people, and particularly because of the repeated denial of the membership of Kljuc municipality in the regional community, by the municipal board, MBO, it is suggested that the municipal assembly at today's decision should adopt the following decision: 1. The earlier decision is confirmed on the joining of Kljuc municipality of the community of municipalities of Banja Luka, and it is established that the Kljuc municipality is a component part of the regional community of Bosanski Krajina, Bosnian Krajina, now called the Autonomous Region of Bosnian Krajina. 2. It is also established that the participation of representatives of the Kljuc municipal assembly in the work of the assembly of the regional community hitherto has been legal and legitimate. The continued membership in the assembly of the autonomous region is confirmed until the election of new deputies. 3. On the basis of this decision, the administrative service of the municipal assembly will draft and submit to the assembly of the autonomous region the appropriate decisions, and the assembly president will sign once again the appropriate documents on membership of the Kljuc municipality in the regional community, that is, the Autonomous Region of Bosnian Krajina. 4. This decision comes into force on the day of its adoption." There's a stamp: "President of the Municipal Assembly, Jovo Banac," signed. And there's a number on the document, 00403770.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. So you can proceed with questioning Dr. Donia on this document. First of all, this document is going to be marked according to your plan P1?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, thank you, P1 -- P1 Alpha, since it's the Serbian version. And hopefully we will have an English translation in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Donia, I'm going to ask you more specific questions on a group of these documents which the others do have English translations. But what is the significance of this document?

Well, this speaks to the decision of the municipal assembly of Kljuc to associate it, itself, or take membership in the ZOBK and at the same time to retain its membership in the Banja Luka municipal association. It's one of several municipalities that voted on the 10th of April to take that step.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'll show you a number of other documents in a moment. But at the time that this decision was made, did the ZOBK actually exist?
If the date on this document is correct, that is, the 10th of April, 1991, at that time it did not exist, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So how would you describe this decision, if the organisation to which it's affiliating itself did not exist?
Well, it's clearly an initiative by a municipality -- municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could now be shown the exhibit which appears in Tab 2. He has his own set. And if the English version of this document could be placed on the ELMO, moved down a little bit, please, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE USHER
utterances.text: Down or up?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, up.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What is this document, Dr. Donia?
This is the decision of the municipal assembly of Titov Drvar to join the ZOBK and subsequent to that, a statement of the reasons that the decision -- or that they made that decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And what is the date of that document?

This is also the 10th of April, 1991. I also should note here that on page 2 of the draft translation is a statement that this initiative began on the 25th of January. And the assembly concluded to enter into contact with other municipalities regarding founding the ZOBK.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And Mr. President, with your permission, I'll mark the B/C/S version of this P2 Alpha, and the English version P2 Bravo, although, actually, in the binders, they are double-sided photocopied documents, simply to save paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could now look at the document numbered Tab 2 -- and we can move quite quickly through these documents, and then I'll ask you some questions briefly at the end. Do you have that document in front of you, Dr. Donia?
This is Tab 2 -- Tab 3? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: This is Tab 2. This is the decision by Bosanski Petrovac in this assembly.
Yes. Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court what this document is.
This document dated 10 April 1991 separates the Bosanski Petrovac municipality from the Bihac, that is, the socialist era Bihac community of municipalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Why are you saying 10 April, 1991, because the document that I have here dealing with the separation of the Bosanski Petrovac from the Bihac is dated 26 April, 1991. The one we had before, which was also referred to as tab 2, was an agreement to join the community of Titov Drvar with the community of -- the municipalities of the Bosanska Krajina. Let's clarify this, because in the case of that particular document, you referred to it as being tabbed at tab 2. This you are referring to also as being at tab 2, when in actual fact it's not. We have to draw a line here where tab 1 starts, as Mr. Ackerman pointed out rightly in the very beginning, because the first document is in front of tab 1, and the second document was in front of tab 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: You want me to refer to them on that basis?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's your choice. I'm not going to interfere in that, but we need to have a uniform practice here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Well, I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So if you want us to understand that when you say "document at tab 2" means the document in front of tab 2, we will take it as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Let's say behind the tab, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So this will be document at tab 3 or at tab 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: This document is at tab 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At tab 2. So again I put the question: Why are you saying it's 10 April, because at least the one I have here is dated the 26th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Which document are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The document that the witness just mentioned, that is document -- and you referred to, document on the separation of Bosanski Petrovac municipality from the rest, from the intermunicipal regional community, Bihac intermunicipal regional community.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'll let the witness answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The document that I'm looking at, which is behind tab 2 and before tab 3, is indeed dated 26 April, 1991. At the end of the first paragraph, it's stated that this decision was adopted at its session on 10th of April, 1991. It was quite common practice for these decisions to be logged into the official records of the municipality sometime after the session was actually held.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That explains it, but because before you said the document was dated date 10th April and that confused the issue. You're clear about this now. Okay. Please go ahead, Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: The Bosanski Petrovac document I think also makes clear in the body of the document that the session was held on the 10th of April of 1991; does it not?
Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And I will mark that document, Your Honour, as P3, the English version being P3 Bravo and the original version being P3 Alpha.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I wonder if Mr. Cayley is offering these as exhibits as he goes through them or -- because if I have an objection, I want to know when to lodge it. That's what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: From everything I've seen of the dynamics in this court between the Prosecution and the Defence already and having prosecuted two of these cases before, I can see that in this particular case there are going to be a lot of objections, and I think the quickest way to get through the witness's evidence is to let him go through, speak about the documents. He can't comment on where these documents came from, because he got them from us, but what he can provide are certain elements of authenticity because he is an expert on contemporary events and the documents often reflect events at the time. So it's a matter for you as Judges to consider, whether or not you regard that as evidence relevant to authenticity, but I think the best time to raise objection is simply if I provide a shopping list at the end of all these exhibits and then Mr. Ackerman can raise his objections and indeed Mr. Pitron and Mr. de Roux can lodge their objections at the end of his evidence, and then it can be a matter for you to decide whether they are admitted and whether we as the Prosecutor are going to have to call evidence in respect of each of these documents as to its origin and authenticity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But that was not the question or the point raised by Mr. Ackerman. Actually, Mr. Ackerman was very categoric in his remark. He wants to know what you are actually proposing to do with these documents at this present moment, whether you are exhibiting them now and you are actually giving them an exhibit number, or whether you propose to exhibit them formally later on, and that would affect the moment when the Defence can make objections. On the question of authenticity and that, I mean, yes, we could visit that later on as we go along, taking into consideration what a witness would state in regard in the course of his testimony. But again, that's not the most important at this present moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley's proposal that we deal with it at the end of the process, based on some list he gives us, probably is extraordinarily convenient but I don't think -- it's up to the Chamber but it seems to me it might make it very difficult for the Chamber because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the Chamber, it would not constitute a problem, if it doesn't constitute a problem for the Defence. The only thing is we are asking a witness to make specific reference to exhibits that are not exactly formally exhibited yet. So this is the whole thing. So I would rather find another solution. On the other hand, I realise that if I instruct Mr. Cayley to file these exhibits formally at this present moment, you will come with all sorts of objections at this moment which would, you know, create problems for the Chamber to proceed with the evidence of Mr. -- of Dr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think I could easily live with all these exhibits being presented at one bulk at a time Mr. Cayley has suggested, if that is okay, if that is all right with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I can, Your Honour. We don't have a jury. We have professional judges. And with the understanding that this witness is going to base some of the conclusions you're going to hear based upon documents which may not be authentic, and that's a decision the Chamber will have to make at some point, and I'm confident that if you decide they are not authentic, you can discount his opinion by whatever amount it ought to be discounted on that basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That is obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's fine with me. I just want to make sure there will be a point where I will be able to assert my objections and they will be heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And the problem can be solved, because as you obviously know, I mean, questions as to the authenticity of these documents will not be answered by Dr. Donia. I mean, Dr. Donia may pass comments and give us his opinion sometimes with regard to certain documents, but I don't take it that he is the key witness that will provide the Prosecution with the proof of authenticity of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can I just make one comment on something Mr. Ackerman has just said, that if a document is not admitted by the Chamber, that therefore Dr. Donia's opinion on that particular matter would be ignored? I think that would be, in my respectful submission, wrong because he is an expert. He is familiar with the events of the time and he knows from other sources that the events referred to in the documents were taking place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Legally, you are correct, definitely much more correct than Mr. Ackerman, because admissibility of a document a priori is one thing, a document which has been admitted as a piece of evidence is another, and a question of probative value and authenticity is something that is to be decided after that document has been -- if the document is not proved to be authentic or if there is some doubt as to the authenticity of that document, the document remains in the records of the case but obviously its probative value fizzles into nothing. So it does not amount to the removal of the document from the records of the case. It will remain always there because -- in actual fact, even a decision -- our decisions are subject to appeal in any case. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley obviously misheard me. I didn't say his testimony should be ignored. Your Honours will recall what I said was that you would be prepared to discount his testimony by whatever amount necessary based upon your finding the document was inauthentic, not that you should ignore his whole testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, I think we have a problem to which I referred to earlier and which I had anticipated actually, but at the time the Deputy Registrar assured me of the flexibility and therefore we went ahead. As I understand, if you proceed now with giving these exhibits -- what would in future become exhibits, a new reference number, exhibit number, they will not be in a position to cope. They would rather prefer you to refer to these documents now with the original reference number, and then, once they are formally exhibited, they will be given the exhibit number that you require. I told you that in this, it's not a question of preferences. I would rather have the Deputy Registrar and her staff working in a way which, to them, is convenient and does not create unnecessary problems. Maybe I'm using "unnecessary" unduly here, but I think in any case, it's quarter to 2.00 and we have to stop our hearing today here. Perhaps you can find time to discuss this with the Deputy Registrar, and I am sure that tomorrow morning, when we resume, we would have found a solution. In any case, we are only at the third or fourth document and we can reverse -- we can enter a [inaudible] tomorrow morning and we will revert to whatever is needed to be the practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'd like to make some further representations to you tomorrow, if I may, Mr. President. It seems to me it's even more complicated than what I've just suggested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is something that had been suggested -- what you suggested was something that was suggested to me by my legal staff sometime back, and -- well, I had gone into it and I had anticipated some problems. When you mentioned it today, and I referred it to you, I understood that there wouldn't be any problems, but obviously, I was right in the very beginning. So please try and find a solution. The important thing is that there will be a uniform marking or numbering of the exhibits as we go along this trial, which will be the same for you, for the Bench, for the Chamber, and for the Defence, because there will be references later on to documents, and I want to make sure that we will be referring to the same document and not have to face a confusion at any given moment and waste half an hour or one hour to dig up the document that needs to be referred to. So I leave it in your good hands. I know how capable you are. And you are also assured of the flexibility of the Deputy Registrar and her staff and I'm sure by tomorrow morning you will have found -- anyway, it's not a difficult problem. There is an easy solution to it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I please have the OTP at the Prosecution Office and the Defence counsel just to stay with me after the hearing for five minutes to discuss how to monitor all these documents and exhibits, to help us help you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And to complement that, may I say I had refrained from suggesting this system precisely because I had been almost assured that if a new system is adopted, it needs to be one which would create the least possible problems to the Registry because they have great problems with recording the exhibits, and they have a system which has been in place, at which they are used and which could lead to confusion because we are -- we don't always have the same persons in the courtroom or dealing with the documentation. So the system needs to be uniform from beginning -- from beginning to end. Okay? So I leave it in your good hands, and tomorrow morning, perhaps you could inform the Chamber formally or informally of the outcome of the --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this afternoon I'm going to report to you the system we are going to use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So this hearing is adjourned until tomorrow morning. We will see you again, Dr. Donia. We will start sharp at 9.00 in the morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1.48 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday the 25th day of January, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
